author: South Bay Mom Map
title: The 6 Best Dim Sum Drives from Cupertino, Ranked by Carts and Cha Siu
text:
1 days ago If you live in Cupertino and you've been making the dim sum drive for the real thing, you already know most South Bay halls quietly dropped cart service over the last two years. The traditional cart push now lives in just a handful of dining rooms between De Anza Blvd and McCarthy Ranch. Here's where to point the car on a Saturday with kids and grandparents in tow.
1. Golden Palace (San Jose) — Closest dim sum to Cupertino, sitting directly on S De Anza Blvd at 1146 S De Anza.
Golden Palace Restaurant — photo 3 — Jenny Ku — source Golden Palace Restaurant — photo 2 — Christine Li — source Golden Palace Restaurant — photo 1 — Angelwrath — source Hoodline named it one of the 15 best dim sum spots in San Jose & Silicon Valley. The Mon–Fri small-plate dim sum runs $3.75 a dish — strong value compared to Koi Palace or HL Peninsula. No carts; you order off a menu and dishes are brought out.
2. Grand Dynasty Chinese Seafood (San Jose) — On Bollinger Rd, roughly two miles from the Cupertino city limit and the closest cart-service dim sum around.
Grand Dynasty Chinese Seafood Restaurant — photo 3 — Mei-Ling Chen — source Grand Dynasty Chinese Seafood Restaurant — photo 2 — Jem Le — source Grand Dynasty Chinese Seafood Restaurant — photo 1 — Su San — source Asian Food Tours called it "particularly grand and enjoyable during dim sum hours." Heads up — 18% gratuity is added automatically, per Yelp's 561+ reviewers, so adjust the math when you tip.
3. Mayflower Restaurant (Milpitas) — Same plaza as Ranch 99 on Barber Ln, which means you can stack the dim sum with the weekly grocery run.
Mayflower Seafood Restaurant — photo 3 — Vivian L (Oak tree) — source Mayflower Seafood Restaurant — photo 2 — Lucky Chuck — source Mayflower Seafood Restaurant — photo 1 — ed marshall — source Tripadvisor's April 2026 list flagged it as the top dim sum in Milpitas, with 1,235+ Yelp reviews. Big lot, reservations accepted, menu-order only — no carts.
4. HL Peninsula (Milpitas) — South Bay outpost of the chain whose Castro Valley flagship KRON4 covered as the largest Cantonese restaurant in the U.S. — 28,000 sq ft, around 900 seats.
HL Peninsula Restaurant - Milpitas — photo 3 — Joey Jiang — source HL Peninsula Restaurant - Milpitas — photo 2 — HL Peninsula Restaurant - Milpitas — source HL Peninsula Restaurant - Milpitas — photo 1 — regis kwong — source Carts still circulate at this Milpitas location per recent reviews, which is rare in 2026. A viral TikTok creator called it "100% worth the visit."
5. Koi Palace (Milpitas) — Third location of the Koi Palace family, opened 2014 at 768 Barber Ln; the Daly City flagship earned a Michelin Plate in Michelin's first U.S. Cantonese guide.
Koi Palace - Milpitas — photo 3 — Winson Yong — source Koi Palace - Milpitas — photo 2 — Koi Palace - Milpitas — source Koi Palace - Milpitas — photo 1 — Arthur — source SJtoday says don't miss "the Cha Sui Bao with a sweet, crispy top." Note that cart service ended in late 2024 — it's a paper menu now.
6. Yin Ji Chang Fen (Milpitas) — The boutique pick on N Milpitas Blvd. The U.S. arm of a Guangzhou rice-noodle-roll chain founded in 1958 in the Old Xiguan district, with sister shops in NYC and Toronto. Congee plus chang fen, QR-code ordering, toddler-safe menu — the easiest weekday lunch on this list.
The McCarthy Ranch cluster — Koi Palace, HL Peninsula, Mayflower — is the trip when out-of-town family is visiting and the move is a banquet hall with high chairs and noise level loud enough that toddler shrieks blend in. For a weekday solo run with a kid in the carrier, ten minutes down De Anza to Golden Palace or up I-880 to Yin Ji is the smarter call.
